chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about a traveler who arrived at his family before the decline of the sun, and he had already eaten. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for him to eat anything that day, nor should he have sexual intercourse during the month of Ramadan, if he has a wife.'

key_terms.أَهْلَهُ: His family (specifically his wife in this context)
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: Decline of the sun (midday, start of Dhuhr time)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who returns home during Ramadan before Dhuhr after eating?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that a traveler who returns home before Zawal (midday) after eating must complete the day's fast, a ruling derived from the principle that the obligation to fast attaches once the traveler becomes resident. The Imam specifies that this includes abstaining from food, drink, and sexual intercourse, highlighting the continuity of the fasting state even after the initial breaking of the fast. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between the status of a traveler and a resident regarding the validity and completeness of the Ramadan fast.
